Combine multiple AME chains

Source: R/ame_parallel.R
combine_ame_chains.Rd

Combine multiple AME chains

Usage

combine_ame_chains(chain_list, diagnostics = TRUE)

Arguments

chain_list

List of ame fit objects from multiple chains

diagnostics

Logical; whether to compute convergence diagnostics (default TRUE)

Value

A single ame object with combined chains. Conditional sampler health counts are summed when every chain supplies them. The original conditional counts and joint-move diagnostics are retained in sampler_diagnostics_by_chain; move diagnostics from a single chain are not presented as pooled values. If a chain from an earlier release lacks the numerical/bound decomposition, the combined sampler_health is NULL; its available per-chain records remain accessible.

Author

Cassy Dorff, Shahryar Minhas, Tosin Salau

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
n <- 12
Y <- matrix(rnorm(n * n), n, n); diag(Y) <- NA
# each fit is one chain (chains = 1); combine_ame_chains() pools them
fit1 <- ame(Y, R = 1, nscan = 200, burn = 50, odens = 1, seed = 1, verbose = FALSE, chains = 1)
fit2 <- ame(Y, R = 1, nscan = 200, burn = 50, odens = 1, seed = 2, verbose = FALSE, chains = 1)
pooled <- combine_ame_chains(list(fit1, fit2))
#> 
#> ── MCMC convergence diagnostics 
#> Number of chains: 2
#> Samples per chain: "200, 200"
#> Diagnostics cover regression coefficients and variance components.
#> ✔ Every parameter passes the between-chain check (R-hat at most its threshold).
# }
